evidence: Adds a condition: reads 'exact 1 letter z remains in the same position' as z fixed AND the other four letters deranged ('the z must be fixed in its position, and all other letters are deranged'), so 8400*9/(15120*120) = 1/24. The event only needs z to stay put: enumerating 5-of-9 labelled selections x 5! shuffles gives (5/9)(1/5) = 1/9 -> 10. Its own reading reproduces exactly 1/24, so the arithmetic is fine.

Two-g case counts labelled permutations with 'G1 not in position 1, G2 not in position 2': 5!-2*4!+3! = 78, so a g landing on the other g's original slot counts as success; no g in any original g slot gives 3*2*3! = 36. The write-up claims the labelled count equals 'g's not in first two positions' (false). Enumeration: 6/56 + (30/56)(4/5) + (20/56)(3/10) = 9/14 -> 23; the labelled version gives exactly 43/56.

Requires 'the z must be in the same position in both permutations, and all other letters must be in different positions', so favourable = 8400*D4 = 75,600. The event only asks that z stays put: (5/9)(1/5) = 1/9 -> 10, confirmed by enumeration. The denominator is also wrong (sum of M^2 over z-containing compositions only, 14,000,000), giving 27/5000, but the added derangement condition alone already makes the answer wrong.

Finds the 8 interior perpendicular crossings correctly but rejects the 4 perpendicular pairs sharing a vertex (5-8/10-8, 5-8/5-3, 10-3/10-8, 10-3/5-3), claiming 'the angle between the two diagonals ... would be the internal angle of the decagon at that vertex, which is 144'. That is false: at vertex 8 the angle subtends arc 5..10 = 180 degrees, so it is 90. Regular 10-gon check: 12 perpendicular pairs, all meeting (8 crossings + 4 at vertices).
